chunks: Saʿīd ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Aʿraj narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The most beloved land to Allah, Exalted is He, is Makkah, and no soil is more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, than its soil; no stone is more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, than its stone; no tree is more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, than its tree; no mountains are more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, than its mountains; and no water is more beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, than its water.

key_terms.أَحَبُّ: most beloved; indicating highest rank in divine favor
key_terms.تُرْبَةٌ: soil or earth; referring to the ground of Makkah
key_terms.جِبَالٌ: mountains; referring to the mountains surrounding Makkah
key_terms.حَجَرٌ: stone; referring to the stones of Makkah
key_terms.شَجَرٌ: tree; referring to the trees of Makkah
key_terms.مَاءٌ: water; referring to the water of Makkah
key_terms.مَكَّةُ: Makkah, the sacred city described here as the most beloved land to Allah

ai.seo_question: Why is Makkah described as the most beloved land to Allah?
ai.summary: This hadith states the special sanctity and divine favor of Makkah, declaring it the most beloved land to Allah. It emphasizes that everything associated with it—its soil, stones, trees, mountains, and water—shares in that honored status, highlighting the sacred rank of the place central to hajj.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2304 - Saeed ibn Abdullah Al-A'raj narrated from Abu Abdullah (as):

"The most beloved land to Allah (swt), the Exalted, is Mecca, and no soil is more beloved to Him, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, than its soil; no stone is more beloved to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, than its stones; no tree is more beloved to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, than its trees; no mountains are more beloved to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, than its mountains; and no water is more beloved to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, than its water."
